### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **7** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **90** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **71** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c1fae16155aeb5364948ecabe6f1307f981c73bd` — the merge of head `3948deb57d550d78daa82fb36450d3b57dc68ceb` into base `1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c1fae16155aeb5364948ecabe6f1307f981c73bd && git checkout c1fae16155aeb5364948ecabe6f1307f981c73bd
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4 3948deb57d550d78daa82fb36450d3b57dc68ceb && git checkout -B drift-repro 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4 && git merge --no-ff 3948deb57d550d78daa82fb36450d3b57dc68ceb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1216abf1a63135359b988a19bb620ea78421fea4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Local-runs: probe — one worktree at head (install, `OS_SKIP_DTS=1` build closure of runtime/rest/cloud-connection/service-automation/dogfood): the touched suites, one ablation of the core switch, and three uncommitted scratch pins confirming must-fix 1–3; worktree removed
Scope: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts, packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-read.ts, packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/no-package-scoped-reads.testkit.ts, packages/runtime/src/flow-slot-view.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation-address.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/runtime/src/endpoint-executor.ts, packages/runtime/src/dispatcher-plugin.ts, and the 15 test files of the diff + read for context: packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts, packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts, ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/FlowRunner.tsx

### ① Derived judgments
- **The switch is one stroke.** `flow` joins `NAMESPACE_SCOPED_BARE_NAME_TYPES`, `PACKAGE_SLOTTED_STORE_TYPES` and `PACKAGE_SCOPED_READ_TYPES`.
- **Ablation** (drop `flow` from the core set): core 1, objectql flow-family 6 and cloud-connection 1 go red. Restored, the tree is clean.
- **Touched suites at head, all green:** core 28, metadata 386, objectql 310, runtime 75, rest 16, cloud-connection 7, service-automation slots and triggers 47, dogfood flow-family 18.
- **The body's table:** rows 1–9 and 11–13 hold in the code and are pinned where the body says. Row 10 does not (must-fix 1).
- **Two fail-closed checks hold:** `endpointPackageOf` keeps the bare 409 for a two-held `api` name, and a package-less run row of a shared name is served by neither namespace's address.

### ② Semver level
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is correct; the Claim's `no (narrowing)` is not. Two answers widen: the install door, item seam and boot seal admit another namespace's holder, and `/automation/:ns/:name` serves a shared name. Rows 3–5 narrow, BREAKING.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, `minor` on core, objectql, metadata and runtime, and the ADR-0087 marker are consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags
- **Rows 4–5 narrow beyond the card's literal "co-owners of one namespace".** They follow from ruling 6810580480 item 1 and ADR-0150 D3.
- **CI was still running when read.**

### ④ Design judgment
1. **must-fix: `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts:545`.**
   - What moves: `actionDeclaringPackage(actionDef, call.declaration.obj)` gives a standalone action with no package the package of the object it is bound to. Measured through the real `/actions` door: an unstamped standalone action on a CRM-stamped object, whose target is held by CRM and HR, answers 200 and runs CRM's slot.
   - Why it fails: row 10 declares 409 naming both. This is a silent pick.
   - Fix: only an embedded declaration inherits its object's package. Add a CONTROL pin.
2. **must-fix: `packages/runtime/src/flow-start-admission.ts:372`.** It is reached from `action-execution.ts:2748`, `endpoint-executor.ts:609` and `domains/automation.ts:2944`.
   - What moves: the record-read walk follows `subflow`/`map` callees through the bare `getFlow`. Once another namespace ships a flow named like P's subflow, a non-system start of P's flow that names an input answers 409, while the engine would run P's own subflow. FROM served TO 409, undeclared.
   - Why it fails: ruling 6810580480 item 2 says this case keeps working.
   - Fix: resolve each callee from the calling flow's package, as `resolveFlowKey` does, and pin it at the three doors.
3. **must-fix: `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts:3644`.**
   - What moves: `bareByNameItem` matches every door under `/:name/runs`, so cancel, resume, restore-suspension and screen read under `/automation/:ns/:name/runs/:runId` moved 409 → served. Measured: CRM's own run is acted on, and HR's run under CRM's address is not.
   - Why it fails: three write verbs moved unlisted.
   - Fix: add them to row 6 and the changeset with the widening arm, and pin own-run served / other-run refused for each.
4. **must-fix: resuming P's paused run on a shared name (read, not run).**
   - What moves: MCP `resume_run` (`domains/mcp.ts:1648-1660`) matches `action.target === run.flowName`, but the run carries its slot key. The Console resumes at the bare `/automation/{flow}/runs/{runId}/resume` (`FlowRunner.tsx:9`), which answers 409.
   - Why it fails: P's screen-flow action starts but can no longer be finished by either first-party caller once another namespace installs the name. The body's first-party count of 0 is wrong for this path.
5. **should-fix: `domains/mcp.ts:1021-1026`.** `list_actions` reads the flow through the bare `getFlow`, so P's flow action is listed without `params` on a shared name. Read it through `flowServiceForCaller` with the row's `packageId`.
6. **should-fix: name the cloud `install-local` door in row 1 and the changeset.** Its wire answer moved 422 → 200; it is pinned in `marketplace-install-local-bare-name-conflict.test.ts`, but the door is not named.
7. **nit:** the body's size (1331, 26 files) and its "Landing order" paragraph are stale against the head.

- **The body's "this branch has merged main" line is behind.** `main` moved 13 commits to 67c49d77. The merge is clean.

### ④ Design judgment
1. **Must-fix:** a run paused before its name was shared is stranded.
   - Where: `packages/runtime/src/flow-slot-view.ts:83-89` (`asNamed`) and `:287-306` (`runFlowKeyOf`), over `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts:4969-4978`.
   - What moves: a run paused while its flow name had one holder, after a second namespace installs that name in the same process.
     - FROM: served at the bare run doors and by `resume`.
     - TO: `409` at every bare run door, and `404 RUN_NOT_FOUND` at the holder's own address.
     - Not in the table.
   - Measured on a booted stack:
     - alpha's screen flow was started four times through alpha's action (run key = the bare name);
     - `install-local` of a second namespace's flow of that name answered 200;
     - then the bare run read, screen read, resume and cancel answered 409 naming both;
     - `POST /automation/alpha/NAME/runs/RUN/resume` answered `404 RUN_NOT_FOUND`, and the run stayed paused;
     - MCP `resume_run` still finished its run.
   - Why: the engine moves `suspendedRuns` to the new key but not the `executionLogs` ring.
     - So `getRun` (`run-history.ts:324-328`) keeps answering the start key. `listSuspendedRuns` carries `PACKAGE/NAME` at that moment.
     - The runtime reads `getRun` first, sees a run "carrying no package", and refuses.
   - Round-2 delta: with the lone-slot line of `asNamed` ablated (round-1 behaviour), both the holder's own address and the newcomer's address resumed the run. The newcomer read alpha's screen and resumed alpha's run.
     - So the round-2 line closes a real hole.
     - It also closes the holder's own door.
   - Why it fails:
     - R2-D says the Console keeps working with a second namespace installed. It also says to stop and report if the run's package cannot be read from the run row.
     - Here the run's package cannot be read, yet the report says it can.
     - Rows 6 and 14 are true only for runs started after the name became shared.
   - Fix: make the run's key follow the move, by either route below. The engine fix also covers finished runs in the ring.
     - Re-key the ring entries in `moveFlowRecords`. This follows the engine's own rule that every per-flow record is filed under the slot key.
     - Or read a run's key from the suspended-run list before `getRun`, in both readers.
   - Pin on a booted stack: pause a run on one holder, then install the second namespace. Then check:
     - the bare screen read and resume are served;
     - the holder's address is served;
     - the newcomer's address is answered as nobody's;
     - MCP `resume_run` is admitted by the holder's action only.
2. **Should-fix:** `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:1668-1669`.
   - A run whose key carries no package skips the package check. So any flow action targeting the name is a candidate, another holder's included.
   - It is reachable in the state of must-fix 1 and in the lone-slot window.
   - When the bare name is refused and the run carries no package, read the package from the suspended entry or refuse.
3. **Nit:** row 6 of the body should name the lone-slot case, as the changeset does.
4. **Nit:** the body's 维护者速读 line "本分支已合 main" should be refreshed to the merge base it names.
